question: The study of the multifunctional severity of COPD is performed with the BODEX and BODE indices, which have some common criteria. Which of the following criteria is exclusively part of one of the two indexes?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "BODEX index" -> "includes dyspnea assessment (MRC)" -> "not exclusive to BODEX" -> 80%
CHAIN: "BODE index" -> "includes distance traveled (meters)" -> "not exclusive to BODE" -> 80%
CHAIN: "BODEX index" -> "includes body mass index (BMI)" -> "not exclusive to BODEX" -> 80%
CHAIN: "BODE index" -> "includes forced vital capacity (FVC)" -> "not exclusive to BODE" -> 80%
CHAIN: "BODEX index" -> "excludes forced vital capacity (FVC)" -> "FVC is part of BODE" -> 90%
CHAIN: "BODE index" -> "excludes dyspnea assessment (MRC)" -> "MRC is part of BODEX" -> 90%
CHAIN: "BODEX index" -> "excludes distance traveled (meters)" -> "meters is part of BODE" -> 90%
CHAIN: "BODEX index" -> "excludes body mass index (BMI)" -> "BMI is part of BODE" -> 90%
analysis: The BODE index includes Body mass index (BMI), Obstruction (measured by FEV1), Dyspnea (MRC scale), and Exercise capacity (6-minute walk distance). The BODEX index is similar but includes the same components with the addition of exacerbation history. The Forced Vital Capacity (FVC) is not a criterion in either index. Therefore, the criterion that is exclusively part of one of the two indices is the Dyspnea assessment (MRC), which is part of the BODE index but not specifically mentioned in the BODEX index. However, since both indices assess dyspnea, the unique criterion is the distance traveled (meters) which is specifically part of the BODE index and not the BODEX index. Thus, the answer is the distance traveled (meters).
